title: Google Fonts — QA Guide (understanding ERROR/FAIL/WARN/INFO levels)
explanation: Explains the severity hierarchy used by Fontspector/Fontbakery and how to read it without panicking.

title: Fontspector — official repository and documentation
explanation: The repository for the QA tool used to generate the report included in this guide: list of checks, available profiles, installation.

title: OpenType Specification — Microsoft Typography
explanation: The complete technical reference for the OpenType format: tables, structure, requirements — useful for understanding where a technical FAIL comes from.

title: Google Fonts — Overall font files requirements
explanation: Google Fonts' baseline technical requirements for any font submission — glyph sets, naming, hinting expectations — a solid general pre-flight checklist.

title: Google Fonts — METADATA file
explanation: How to fill out the METADATA.pb file Google Fonts expects (family name, category, designer, subsets) — a common source of metadata FAILs.

title: Google Fonts — Vertical metrics
explanation: Explains vertical metrics (ascender, descender, line gap, win/hhea/typo values) and why mismatches between them cause clipped or inconsistent line spacing across platforms.

title: Typeface name check
explanation: A quick lookup tool to check whether a typeface name is already registered, before committing to it in your naming metadata.

title: fontTools & ttx
explanation: The Python toolkit (and its ttx command-line converter) most font QA scripts are built on — useful for inspecting exactly what's inside a binary font's tables.

title: FontDev — browser-based font table inspector
explanation: Drop a font in and browse its raw OpenType tables directly in the browser, without installing anything.

title: Font Analyzer
explanation: A free web tool that scans a font for technical issues across character sets, language support, metrics, kerning and OpenType features in a single pass.

title: Google Fonts — Outline Quality
explanation: A detailed breakdown of common outline problems — missing extrema, wrong contour direction, overlapping paths, fractional coordinates — with before/after examples of what breaks on export.

title: Drawing good paths (Glyphs tutorial)
explanation: Glyphs' own tutorial on constructing clean, well-behaved Bézier paths — the habits that prevent most outline QA fails before they happen.

title: Drawing Vectors for Type & Lettering
explanation: A practical look at vector drawing technique for letterforms, from Ohno Type Co.

title: How to draw with FontForge
explanation: FontForge's own guide to its drawing tools, for anyone constructing outlines directly rather than importing artwork.

title: Google Fonts — Diacritic marks
explanation: The single most complete reference here: design consistency across accents, legacy vs. combining marks, anchor naming conventions, Vietnamese tone stacking, soft-dotted substitution, and the dotted-circle glyph — illustrated with right/wrong comparisons.

title: diacritics.typo.cz
explanation: Filip Blažek's long-running reference on designing correct Latin accents, still one of the most cited resources on the topic.

title: Context of Diacritics
explanation: A frequency analysis of which Latin languages use which diacritics, and how often — useful for prioritizing which accents actually matter for a given language target.

title: On diacritics
explanation: David Březina's general introduction to designing diacritics, covering the design reasoning behind the rules rather than just the rules themselves.

title: The Insects Project
explanation: A resource focused specifically on Central European diacritics — the accents that trip up designers who only tested Western European languages.

title: Microsoft Character Design Standards
explanation: Microsoft's own character design guidelines covering the Latin alphabet, figures, diacritics, punctuation and symbols — a solid baseline reference for consistent construction.

title: How to draw a Capital Sharp S
explanation: Ralf Herrmann's guide specifically on drawing the capital ẞ, including where designers most commonly get its proportions wrong.

title: How to Draw a Proper Capital Eszett
explanation: A second, independent walkthrough of capital eszett construction — useful to cross-check against the guide above, since conventions here are still debated.

title: Vietnamese Typography — Tone Marks
explanation: Donny Trương's comprehensive reference on Vietnamese typography, with a dedicated section on tone marks — exactly the stacking and collision issues that come up most.

title: Cyrillic local forms
explanation: Maria Doreuli explains which Cyrillic letterforms need localized shapes rather than a direct trace of the Latin design.

title: How to design Cyrillic letters Њ (Nje), Љ (Lje), Ћ (Tshe), and Ђ (Dje)
explanation: A worked walkthrough of constructing the Serbian/Macedonian-specific letters Њ, Љ, Ћ and Ђ, which don't map cleanly onto other Cyrillic letters.

title: Greek type design
explanation: Gerry Leonidas' overview of what makes Greek letterforms distinct from a Latin-based approach to the same shapes.

title: Polytonic Greek: a guide for type designers
explanation: Irene Vlachou's guide to polytonic Greek — the accent system used for historical and liturgical Greek text, well beyond what monotonic Greek requires.

title: Mark to mark positioning (Glyphs tutorial)
explanation: Glyphs' tutorial on setting up mark-to-mark anchors, for when one diacritic needs to stack on top of another.

title: HarfBuzz — what is it?
explanation: The text-shaping engine most platforms actually use to render a font's marks and features — useful background for understanding why an anchor or GDEF problem manifests the way it does.

title: The Raster Tragedy at Low-Resolution Revisited
explanation: The classic, still-required-reading essay on why text renders the way it does at small sizes on screen, and what hinting is actually solving.

title: How to hint variable fonts
explanation: Google Fonts' own guide to hinting variable fonts with VTT, for the cases where the general recommendation to leave VFs unhinted doesn't apply.

title: Kern On
explanation: Tim Ahrens' kerning tool, built around comparing a font's spacing against its own established rhythm rather than fixed rules.

title: HTLetterspacer
explanation: An automated spacing tool from Huerta Tipográfica that suggests sidebearings based on the shapes of the glyphs themselves.

title: kerncritic
explanation: Simon Cozens' tool for auditing an existing kerning table for suspicious or inconsistent pairs.

title: Google Fonts — Variable fonts specifics
explanation: Google Fonts' full variable-font requirements: filename conventions, the STAT table, fvar instances, and the 'font origin' concept that explains many confusing QA fails.

title: Google Fonts — Axis Registry Protocol
explanation: The protocol for getting a custom variable axis recognized by Google Fonts' Axis Registry, for fonts that use one beyond the standard weight/width/etc.

title: Axis Praxis
explanation: A browser playground for testing how a variable font behaves across its full design space, with nothing to install.

title: AGL Specification
explanation: The Adobe Glyph List specification that defines standard glyph-naming conventions — useful when a QA report flags an oddly-named or unrecognized glyph.

title: Fonts and Layout for Global Scripts
explanation: A free, thorough book by Simon Cozens on Unicode, OpenType shaping and how complex scripts actually get laid out — background reading for anything mark-positioning related.

title: SIL Font Development Best Practices
explanation: SIL's field-tested notes on font production for minority and lesser-resourced languages, covering encoding and process questions that rarely come up in mainstream guides.

title: Words of Type
explanation: A community-maintained glossary of type and font-engineering terminology, handy when a QA report uses a term you don't recognize.

title: Microsoft Typography Docs
explanation: Microsoft's documentation hub for everything typography-related, including the OpenType spec and font-development guidance.

title: Apple's TrueType Reference Manual
explanation: Apple's own low-level reference for the TrueType format — tables, hinting instructions, glyph outlines — for when a problem needs a from-the-source answer.

title: Adobe's Font Tech Notes
explanation: A collection of Adobe's historical technical notes on font formats and naming conventions, still referenced for edge cases the newer specs gloss over.

title: OpenType Font Variations Overview
explanation: Microsoft's explanation of how variable fonts actually work under the hood — useful for understanding the 'font origin' concept, which trips up a lot of QA fails.

title: A Variable Fonts Primer
explanation: A gentle, visual introduction to variable font technology for anyone who needs the concept explained before diving into axis registries and STAT tables.

title: MDN Variable Fonts Guide
explanation: Mozilla's developer-facing guide to variable fonts, useful when the question is how a browser will actually read your font's axes.

title: Eszett (ẞ) — Lucas Fonts
explanation: Lucas de Groot's design notes on the capital ß — a third, independent take worth comparing against the other two eszett guides here.

title: Polish diacritics how-to
explanation: Adam Twardoch's detailed reference on Polish-specific diacritics, for when the general Latin-accent guides above aren't specific enough.

title: Extending Cyrillic (and later Latin) character sets
explanation: Thomas Phinney on how Cyrillic character-set extensions were historically defined — useful context for why some Cyrillic glyph sets are shaped the way they are.

title: The relatively easy way to find out the quality of a Cyrillic typeface
explanation: Alexandra Korolkova's checklist-style piece for quickly spotting whether a font's Cyrillic was designed with care or just auto-generated from the Latin.

title: ttfautohint
explanation: FreeType's automated hinting tool and its documentation — the most common way fonts get usable TrueType hinting without doing it by hand.

title: RoboFont documentation
explanation: Official documentation for RoboFont's UFO-based, scriptable font-editing workflow.

title: FontLab help & tutorials
explanation: FontLab's official help center, covering drawing, hinting, OpenType features and more inside the editor.

title: Monotype's Foundry Support
explanation: Monotype's support portal for foundries, with production and technical guidance for getting fonts market-ready.
